Libraries:

```{r}

library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(dplyr)
library(JADE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(moments)
```

Load the 3-variate spatial dataset.

```{r}
data <- st_read("data/processed/londonCRE.gpkg", quiet=TRUE)
```

We build the spatial kernel functions which we will utilize for SBSS, spFOBI and spJADE.

```{r}
library(dbscan)
library(Matrix)
library(RSpectra)

# 1. Project to meters
cre <- st_transform(data, crs = 27700)
coords <- st_coordinates(cre)
n <- nrow(coords)

# 2. Define bandwidths (phi) in meters
phi_values <- c(100, 250, 500, 1000)

# 3. Build Truncated Sparse Exponential Kernels
kernel_list_raw <- lapply(phi_values, function(phi) {
  
  # An exponential curve has a fatter tail than a Gaussian curve.
  # We extend the cutoff to 5 * phi to safely capture the spatial signal 
  # before truncating. (at 5*phi, the spatial weight is exp(-5) ≈ 0.006)
  cutoff_dist <- 5 * phi 
  
  # Use the highly optimized KD-Tree to find neighbors within the new cutoff
  nn <- dbscan::frNN(coords, eps = cutoff_dist)
  
  # Extract indices and distances
  i <- rep(1:n, lengths(nn$id))
  j <- unlist(nn$id)
  d <- unlist(nn$dist)
  
  # Apply the Exponential decay formula: f(d) = exp(-d / phi)
  weights <- exp(-d / phi)
  
  # Build the sparse symmetric matrix
  W_sparse <- sparseMatrix(
    i = i, 
    j = j, 
    x = weights, 
    dims = c(n, n), 
    symmetric = FALSE 
  )
  
  # Add the self-relationship (distance = 0, exp(0) = 1) to the diagonal
  diag(W_sparse) <- 1
  
  return(W_sparse)
})

# 4. Fast Spectral Normalization using Arnoldi Iteration
spectral_normalize_sparse <- function(kernels) {
  lapply(kernels, function(kmat) {
    
    # Standard eigen() calculates ALL 21,000 eigenvalues (O(N^3)).
    # RSpectra::eigs_sym only calculates the top 1 eigenvalue directly.
    # On an M1, this reduces computation time from hours to milliseconds.
    max_eigen <- RSpectra::eigs_sym(kmat, k = 1, which = "LA")$values
    
    if (max_eigen == 0) max_eigen <- 1 
    
    return(kmat / max_eigen)
  })
}

kernel_list <- spectral_normalize_sparse(kernel_list_raw)
```

Prepare the data:

```{r}
X <- data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(Value, Volatility, Liquidity) %>%
  as.matrix()

n <- nrow(X)
kernel_list <- c(list(Matrix::Diagonal(n)), kernel_list)

# 2. Calculate the scaling factors (Sf_list)
# This works perfectly on sparse matrices from the Matrix package
Sf_list <- lapply(kernel_list, function(kmat) {
  sum(kmat) / nrow(kmat)
})
```

For SBSS we do not pass the $f_0$ kernel.

```{r}
sbss_res <- sbss(x=X, kernel_list=kernel_list[-1])
print(sbss_res$w)
```

Now we run the FOBI and JADE methods for iid observations:

```{r}
fobi_res <- FOBI(X)
print(fobi_res$W)

jade_res <- JADE(X)
print(jade_res$W)
```

Now we run spFOBI and spJADE with the $f_0$ kernel.

```{r}
source("src/spICA.R")
```

```{r}
spjade_res <- spjade(
  x = X, 
  kernel_list = kernel_list, 
  Sf_list = Sf_list
)
print(spjade_res$w)
```

```{r}
spfobi_res <- spfobi(
  x = X,
  kernels = kernel_list
)
print(spfobi_res$w)
```

We compute statistics between the different methods:\

```{r}
library(spdep)

# 1. Define the specific bandwidth you want to test (e.g., the 1000m scale)
phi_test <- 1000
cutoff_dist <- 5 * phi_test # Match the 5*phi tail we used in spJADE

# 2. Extract neighbors using the extended cutoff
nb_tail <- dnearneigh(coords, d1 = 0, d2 = cutoff_dist)
dist_list <- nbdists(nb_tail, coords)

# 3. Apply the EXACT Exponential decay function used during extraction
exp_list <- lapply(dist_list, function(d) exp(-d / phi_test))

# 4. Create the listw object
# We retain style = "W" specifically to stabilize the global Moran's I variance, 
# but the relative weights inside the rows now perfectly match your spJADE model.
listw_exp <- nb2listw(nb_tail, glist = exp_list, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
```

```{r}
sources_list <- list(
  "FOBI"   = fobi_res$S, 
  "JADE"   = jade_res$S, 
  "spJADE" = spjade_res$s,
  "spFOBI" = spfobi_res$s
)
```

```{r}
cre_projected <- st_transform(cre, 3857)
london <- get_tiles(cre_projected, provider="CartoDB.PositronNoLabels", zoom=11)
```

Independent component 1

```{r}
# Calculate a robust upper limit to handle the 38.74 outlier
# We'll set the limit at the 99th percentile of the absolute values
robust_limit <- quantile(abs(cre_projected$spjade_IC1), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

IC1_plot <- ggplot(data = cre_projected) +
  layer_spatial(london) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(color = spjade_IC1), 
    size = 0.8, 
    stroke = 0
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#5E3C99",    
    mid = "#F7F7F7",    # Neutral White for near-zero
    high = "#E66101",   # Burnt Orange for positive
    midpoint = 0,       # The most important argument
    name = NULL,
    limits = c(-robust_limit, robust_limit),
    oob = scales::squish
  ) +
  theme_void() + 
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.93, 0.08),
    legend.justification = c("right", "bottom"))

print(IC1_plot)
```

```{r}

W_sbss <- coef(sbss_res) 

loadings_sbss <- solve(W_sbss)

W_fobi <- coef(fobi_res)

W_jade <- coef(jade_res)

W_spjade <- coef(spjade_res)

loadings_spfobi <- solve(W_spfobi)
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Helper function
prepare_heatmap_data <- function(loadings_mat, model_name) {
  colnames(loadings_mat) <- paste0("IC", 1:ncol(loadings_mat))
  
  if (is.null(rownames(loadings_mat))) {
    rownames(loadings_mat) <- paste0("Var", 1:nrow(loadings_mat))
  }
  
  df <- as.data.frame(loadings_mat)
  df$Variable <- factor(rownames(df), levels = rev(rownames(df))) 
  
  df_long <- pivot_longer(df, 
                          cols = starts_with("IC"), 
                          names_to = "Component", 
                          values_to = "Loading")
  
  df_long$Model <- model_name
  
  return(df_long)
}

# 2. Process all five models
df_sbss   <- prepare_heatmap_data(loadings_sbss, "1. SBSS")
df_fobi   <- prepare_heatmap_data(loadings_fobi, "2. FOBI")
df_jade   <- prepare_heatmap_data(loadings_jade, "3. JADE")
df_spfobi <- prepare_heatmap_data(loadings_spfobi, "4. spFOBI")
df_spjade <- prepare_heatmap_data(loadings_spjade, "5. spJADE")

# 3. Combine into one master dataset
all_loadings <- bind_rows(df_sbss, df_fobi, df_jade, df_spfobi, df_spjade)

# 4. THE FIX: Normalize strictly within each Model AND Variable (Row-wise)
all_loadings <- all_loadings %>%
  group_by(Model, Variable) %>% # <--- Changed from Component to Variable
  mutate(Norm_Loading = Loading / max(abs(Loading))) %>%
  ungroup()

# 5. Generate the faceted heatmap
heatmap_plot <- ggplot(all_loadings, aes(x = Component, y = Variable, fill = Norm_Loading)) +
  geom_tile(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.5) + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-1, 1),
                       name = "Loadings") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, nrow = 1) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = "",
    x = "Latent Component",
    y = "Observed Variable"
  )

# Display the plot
print(heatmap_plot)
```

Mutual independence

```{r}
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(knitr)

# Helper function to get the top 3 Moran's I values
get_top3_morans <- function(data, prefix, weights) {
  df_clean <- st_drop_geometry(data)
  
  # FIX 1: Ignore case and drop the strict "_IC" requirement to match names like "spJADE_1"
  cols <- grep(paste0("^", prefix), names(df_clean), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  
  # SAFETY CATCH: If columns still aren't found, stop and print exactly why
  if (length(cols) == 0) {
    stop(paste("No columns found in the dataset starting with:", prefix))
  }
  
  # FIX 2: unlist() ensures the result is an atomic vector, and drop = FALSE 
  # prevents subsetting issues if only one column accidentally matches
  morans <- unlist(sapply(df_clean[, cols, drop = FALSE], function(x) {
    moran.test(x, weights)$estimate[1] 
  }))
  
  # Sort decreasing and return exactly the first 3 values
  top3 <- sort(morans, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
  return(top3)
}

# Construct the results data frame
results_all_morans <- data.frame(
  Methodology = c("spJADE", "spFOBI", "JADE", "FOBI"),
  IC1 = c(
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spjade", listw_exp)[1],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spfobi", listw_exp)[1],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "jade", listw_exp)[1],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "fobi", listw_exp)[1] # Make sure "fobi" is your actual prefix
  ),
  IC2 = c(
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spjade", listw_exp)[2],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spfobi", listw_exp)[2],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "jade", listw_exp)[2],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "fobi", listw_exp)[2]
  ),
  IC3 = c(
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spjade", listw_exp)[3],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "spfobi", listw_exp)[3],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "jade", listw_exp)[3],
    get_top3_morans(cre_projected, "fobi", listw_exp)[3]
  )
)

# Generate the LaTeX code
kable(results_all_morans, 
      format = "latex", 
      booktabs = TRUE, 
      digits = 4, 
      col.names = c("Methodology", "Component 1", "Component 2", "Component 3"),
      caption = "Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's $I$) decay profile across the first three extracted components.",
      label = "tab:morans_decay",
      escape = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(knitr)

# Helper function to get the top 3 absolute excess kurtosis values
get_top3_kurtosis <- function(data, prefix) {
  df_clean <- st_drop_geometry(data)
  cols <- grep(paste0("^", prefix, "_IC"), names(df_clean), value = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate absolute excess kurtosis for all components
  kurts <- sapply(df_clean[, cols], function(x) {
    n <- length(x)
    mean_x <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    sd_x <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    # Excess kurtosis formula
    kurt <- sum((x - mean_x)^4, na.rm = TRUE) / (n * sd_x^4) - 3
    return(abs(kurt))
  })
  
  # Sort decreasing and return exactly the first 3 values
  top3 <- sort(kurts, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
  return(top3)
}

# Construct the results data frame
results_all_kurts <- data.frame(
  Methodology = c("Standard JADE", "Standard FOBI","Spatial JADE"),
  IC1 = c(
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "jade")[1],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "spjade")[1],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "fobi")[1]
  ),
  IC2 = c(
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "jade")[2],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "spjade")[2],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "fobi")[2]
  ),
  IC3 = c(
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "jade")[3],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "spjade")[3],
    get_top3_kurtosis(cre_projected, "fobi")[3]
  )
)

# Generate the LaTeX code
kable(results_all_kurts, 
      format = "latex", 
      booktabs = TRUE, 
      digits = 4, 
      col.names = c("Methodology", "Component 1", "Component 2", "Component 3"),
      caption = "Absolute excess kurtosis ($|\\kappa|$) profile across the top three extracted components. Higher values indicate stronger isolation of non-Gaussian economic signals.",
      label = "tab:kurtosis_profile",
      escape = FALSE)
```
